dinemetric.title: Dinemetric
dinemetric.description: An AI-powered restaurant platform with menu recommendations and insights to support daily operations.
dinemetric.problem: Restaurants often have customer, menu, and operational data spread across different sources, making it difficult to turn that information into useful insights and actionable recommendations.
dinemetric.decision:
The application uses a modern full-stack architecture with Next.js and TypeScript for the frontend and application layer, Supabase for authentication and database functionality, and API integrations for AI-powered features.

Separating the application into reusable UI, data-access, and backend workflows helped keep features maintainable while supporting continued product development.
dinemetric.contribution:
Contributed to the development of Dinemetric, an AI-powered restaurant analytics platform built with Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, and modern full-stack technologies.

My work included developing and improving application features, integrating frontend components with backend services and database workflows, debugging full-stack issues, and supporting AI-powered functionality that transforms restaurant data into structured insights and recommendations.

I also worked with API-driven workflows and application state to ensure data could move reliably between the user interface, backend services, database, and AI features.
dinemetric.outcome: The platform provides restaurant teams with a centralized way to work with business data and AI-generated insights, helping turn complex information into more understandable and actionable recommendations.

smilysis.title: Smilysis
smilysis.description: An application for tracking dental habits and progress with AI-powered scans and personalized insights.
smilysis.problem: Bring dental habits, scan-based insights, and oral-health progress into one tracking experience.
smilysis.decision: Uses a shared Supabase client with session persistence so sign-in state can be reused across the application.
smilysis.contribution: Contributed to the team developing Smilysis, a dental-health tracking application. The product brings together daily habits, scan-based insights, and personalized progress tracking.
smilysis.outcome: The application brings dental habits, scan-based insights, and oral-health progress into one experience.

sips.title: Sips Cafe
sips.description: A bubble tea ordering platform with menu browsing, payments, and administration tools.
sips.problem: Sips Cafe needed a web-based ordering system that could manage menu items, customization options, customer accounts, orders, and online payments within a single application.
sips.decision:
I designed the application around relational entities representing menu items, orders, customization options, users, and transactions.

Separating these concerns through ASP.NET Core MVC, Entity Framework Core, and structured database relationships made it easier to manage complex order customization while maintaining data consistency.
sips.contribution:
Designed and developed a full-stack cafe ordering application using ASP.NET Core MVC, C#, Entity Framework Core, and a relational database.

I implemented user authentication and authorization, email verification, reCAPTCHA protection, menu and product management, customizable drink options, shopping-cart functionality, and order processing.

I also designed REST-based application workflows, created relational data models for products, orders, transactions, and customization options, and integrated PayPal Checkout for online payments.

Administrative functionality was added to support role-based access and management of menu items and application data.
sips.outcome: The completed application supports the full customer ordering workflow—from account creation and customized product selection through checkout and payment—while also providing administrative functionality for managing menu data and orders.
